## What's new

Threadnote 4 beta.29 focuses on performance and reliability in large monorepos and concurrent agent orchestrators.

- Multiple agents can now use linked Git worktrees concurrently without sharing dirty source state. Extraction runs in
  parallel, worktree overlays and active graph pointers stay isolated, and only the short publication step is
  serialized.
- Recall vector work is fenced to the lexical corpus generation that requested it. Stale waiters cannot replace a
  newer generation, semantic scoring cannot mix generations, and bounded churn falls back to coherent lexical recall.
- One-file graph updates can reuse a versioned clean-snapshot receipt across sessions. Eligible edits stage and resolve
  only their changed facts instead of hydrating the complete graph into temporary tables; uncertain declaration,
  workspace, alias, or file-set changes still rebuild conservatively.
- Graph builders, readers, maintenance, repair, purge, parser-cache cleanup, and vector publication now coordinate with
  process-aware locks and snapshot leases. Interrupted work remains reusable, while stale and PID-reused owners are
  reclaimed safely.
- Large-repository status is more informative. Manager and CLI report active phases, owner/waiter state, calibrated
  estimates when enough evidence exists, and faster active polling without continuously waking idle repositories.
- `threadnote graph stats` exposes SQLite main/WAL/SHM and reclaimable-page information, while
  `threadnote graph compact --dry-run` previews safe compaction with free-space and active-builder checks.
- `threadnote processes` reports a bounded privacy-safe inventory of Threadnote parents, model workers, MCP sessions,
  and graph activity. Local-model workers now use single-flight restart, bounded retry, and five-minute idle eviction.
- Parser facts remain content-addressed and reusable, while resolution inputs carry independent derivation identities.
  Cached and fresh extraction are checked for equivalence across TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Swift, schemas, manifests,
  rationale comments, barrels, overloads, and multi-file references.
- The benchmark harness now records phase-level CPU, RSS, SQLite/WAL growth, lifecycle checkpoints, sampler readiness,
  and failure artifacts. The enforced 10k-symbol development run keeps the fast cross-session incremental path within
  its reviewed budget; the full production-shaped profile remains an opt-in scheduled artifact.
- The website now documents Conductor-style multi-worktree workflows, adds an animated parallel-agent pro tip, and
  explains generation-safe recall and lexical-only fallback. The landing animation also uses the current Three.js timer
  API without browser deprecation warnings.

Existing beta installations can update in place:

```bash
threadnote update --beta
```

Fresh beta installation:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kashkovsky/threadnote/v4.0.0-beta.29/scripts/install.sh |
  sh -s -- --beta
```
